glossary.luminal obstruction: A blockage inside the hollow channel of an organ, here the appendix.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as WCC and CRP that rise with inflammation or infection.
glossary.vomiting: Forceful bringing up of stomach contents.
glossary.fever: Body temperature above about 38 degrees C.
glossary.swinging pyrexia: A fever that rises and falls repeatedly through the day, typical of a collection of pus.
glossary.drainage: Letting pus out of an abscess, often with a needle or drain placed under imaging.
glossary.hyperextension: Moving a joint backwards beyond its normal straight position.
glossary.internal rotation: Turning a limb inwards towards the midline.
glossary.pelvic appendix: An appendix that hangs down into the pelvis, near the obturator internus muscle.
glossary.urine dip: A dipstick test of urine for blood, protein, leucocytes and nitrites.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan of the body.
glossary.contrast: A dye given into a vein or by mouth so organs and vessels show up better on a scan.
glossary.equivocal: Uncertain; neither clearly positive nor clearly negative.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given through a vein to replace losses and keep the patient hydrated.
glossary.anti-emetics: Drugs that stop nausea and vomiting.
glossary.prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat one that has started.
glossary.amoxicillin: A penicillin antibiotic that covers many gut bacteria.
glossary.definitive treatment: The treatment that deals with the actual cause, not just the symptoms.
glossary.perforated appendicitis: Appendicitis where the inflamed wall has burst, releasing pus and bacteria.
glossary.generalised peritonitis: Inflammation spread across the whole peritoneal lining, not just one area.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.intraluminal pressure: The pressure inside the hollow centre of the organ.
glossary.venous drainage: Blood flowing out of a tissue through the veins.
glossary.arterial supply: Blood flowing into a tissue through the arteries.
glossary.bacterial overgrowth: Too many bacteria multiplying in a blocked space.
glossary.ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, starving it of oxygen.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the full thickness of an organ wall.
glossary.distension: Swelling or stretching of a hollow organ.
glossary.referred pain: Pain felt at a site away from its source because they share nerve supply.
glossary.autonomic innervation: Nerve supply from the automatic nervous system, which gives vague, poorly localised gut pain.
glossary.peritoneal irritation: Inflammation of the peritoneal lining that makes it painful to stretch or move.
glossary.wall off: When the body surrounds infection, often with omentum, to stop it spreading.
glossary.palpation: Examining by feeling with the hands.
